title: Choose the Settings structure
question: All three preserve every current setting. Choose how General, Meetings, and Appearance should reveal their depth.

options.label: Meeting Lifecycle
options.thesis: Organize settings around what happens before, during, and after a meeting, with current status visible at the top.
options.viewport: A compact pane switcher sits beside the page title; a health strip leads into Before, During, and After cards, each showing only its essential controls until expanded.
options.risk: Provider-specific options move one level deeper because lifecycle takes precedence over technology names.

options.label: Essentials + Advanced
options.thesis: Give each pane a small set of everyday cards and place every expert workflow in clearly named expandable groups below.
options.viewport: The title and text pane switcher lead into two or three essential cards; a quiet Advanced area below summarizes hidden providers, export, sync, and automation before expansion.
options.risk: Users who tune providers frequently make an extra click, though their last expanded state can be remembered.

options.label: Preferences Rail
options.thesis: Use a compact native subcategory rail so only one focused settings group is visible at a time.
options.viewport: The global pane switcher stays at the top; Meetings adds a narrow left rail for Recording, Transcription, Notes, Calendar, Sharing, and Advanced with one detail surface on the right.
options.risk: It eliminates long scrolling but adds navigation and can make related settings feel farther apart.
